title: Resolve a path through symbolic links
description:
Model how the object manager resolves names. `links` maps symbolic-link names to their targets, for example `"\??\C:"` to `"\Device\HarddiskVolume3"`.

Write `resolve(path, links)`:

- Repeatedly find the **longest** link name that is a prefix of the current path **at a component boundary** (the link name is the whole path, or is followed by `\`). Replace that prefix with the link's target.
- Stop when no link matches, and return the final path.
- If more than 16 replacements happen, the links form a loop: return `std::nullopt`.

```
links:  \??\C:      -> \Device\HarddiskVolume3
        \??\Echo    -> \Device\XenonEcho
resolve("\??\C:\Games\save.dat") = "\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Games\save.dat"
resolve("\??\Echo")              = "\Device\XenonEcho"
resolve("\??\Cx\file")           = "\??\Cx\file"       (\??\C: is not a whole component of \??\Cx)
```
hints: For each link, it matches if the current path starts with the link's name and the next character after it is either the end of the path or a backslash. Keep the longest match.
Replace the matched prefix with the target and loop again; count the replacements, and give up after 16.
lessonTitle: Kernel Objects and the Object Manager
